improv_extras.concept: build a form by CSG boolean ops on SDF primitives (smooth-min union/subtraction) and clothe the resulting surface in particles — a carved, solid object

v1.feedback: The Hepworth pierced-form SDF is well-constructed — the smooth-min unions and boolean cylinder subtractions create a recognizable standing sculpture with interior voids, and the bone/patina palette is perfectly restrained. The breathing displacement at 0.022 amplitude reads as contemplative without being invisible. Two improvements: (1) the chain-from-parent lineage to mvh (disrupt_the_grid) is not legible — there's no visible grid disruption memory or morphing residue, so this reads as a fresh start rather than a mutation; consider retaining a faint grid scaffold or transitional geometry that dissolves into the Hepworth form. (2) The interior void particles could benefit from slightly more depth contrast — darken the voidCol further or increase the alpha falloff inside the bored-out cylinders so the pierced negative space reads more dramatically against the bone exterior.

v2.feedback: Strong concept — Hepworth pierced standing form built from SDF booleans is a legit sculpture reference, and the grid-scaffold-dissolving-into-carved-surface narrative ties cleanly to the parent mvh disrupted grid. The SDF rejection sampling and smooth-min unions are correctly implemented, and the form should fill ~75% of vertical frame at the current camera distance. Two refinements: (1) the three cylinder piercings are all near-horizontal bores — add one vertical or strongly diagonal void to break the parallel read and make the silhouette more distinctive from multiple viewing angles; (2) the grid-to-surface migration should have a visible time progression (early seconds show scaffolding, later seconds show carved stone) rather than a static lerp, so the viewer witnesses the transformation rather than arriving at a finished state.
